title: A grade book
description:
Write a small grade-book module: read students' marks from a file, compute statistics, and write an aligned report.

```python
def parse_line(line): ...                 # "Ada Lovelace: 90, 85, 77" -> ("Ada Lovelace", [90, 85, 77]); None if not valid
def load(path): ...                       # dict name -> list of marks, from every valid line, in file order
def average(marks): ...                   # rounded to one decimal; None for no marks
def letter(avg): ...                      # "A" >= 90, "B" >= 80, "C" >= 70, "D" >= 60, else "F"; "-" for None
def report(book): ...                     # the report text (below)
def save_report(path, book): ...          # writes report(book) to path
```

**Lines**: a name, a colon, then marks separated by commas. Spaces around everything are ignored. Marks are whole numbers from 0 to 100. A line with no colon, an empty name, or any mark that is not a valid number is invalid (`None`); a line with a name and no marks after the colon is valid with an empty list. Blank lines are skipped. A name that appears again replaces the earlier marks.

**The report**, one line per student sorted by average (highest first; students without marks last; ties by name), then a summary:

```
Name            Avg  Grade
Grace Hopper   92.0  A
Ada Lovelace   84.0  B
Linus             -  -
3 students, class average 88.0
```

- The name column is as wide as the longest name or the word `Name`, whichever is longer, plus 3 spaces; the average is right-aligned in 4 characters (`-` when there are no marks); then 2 spaces and the grade. The header uses the same widths (`Avg` right-aligned in 4).
- The class average is the average of the students' averages (students without marks are left out), with one decimal, or `-` if no student has marks.
- Every line ends with a new line.
hints: `line.partition(":")` splits at the first colon into three parts: before, the colon, and after.

Tuples sort item by item: by the first item, and by the second only on a tie. So a list of `(-average, name)` tuples sorts with the highest average first and equal averages by name. Keep the students without marks in a separate list and put them at the end.
`name.ljust(width)` pads text with spaces on the right to a given width, and `text.rjust(4)` pads on the left (lesson 2.01), which is all the alignment the report needs.
requirements: Valid and invalid lines are told apart exactly as described.
Averages, grades and the sort order are correct, including students without marks.
The report is aligned for any name lengths, and can be saved to a file.
stretch: Add a command-line script that takes the marks file and an output file as arguments (lesson 6.04), and a histogram of grades drawn with `#` characters.
